To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the structural and biochemical properties of Mycobacteriurn tuberculosis lysine 5-aminotransfeiase (LAT) are modulated by the active site residue T330 and that the binding mode of the 2-aminornethyI pipenidine derivative is different from that of the natural substrates.
(1) T330 is essential for LAT activity, and its mutation to alanine or serine leads to loss of activity.
the structural analysis of the LAT mutants and the LAT-inhibitor co-crystal structure reveal the structural basis of the LAT activity and inhibition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding of structure-function relationships and inhibitor design for LAT, a potential drug target.
understanding the mechanism of LAT and its inhibition.
the structure and function of the lysine-ɛ-aminooxoadipate pathway of M. tuberculosis and the development of novel inhibitors as potential anti-TB drugs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the LAT active-site residues, E243, T330 and N328 are important in substrate binding and catalysis, and that the inhibitor binding mode is distinct from substrate binding.

the structural and functional analysis of LAT mutants and inhibitor co-crystals has revealed a complex interplay of residues and water molecules in the active site of LAT, which may be useful in the development of novel anti-tuberculosis agents.
the LAT inhibitors identified by us are not specific to LAT and can inhibit a number of PLP-dependent enzymes, including asparagine synthetase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
LAT has two distinct binding modes and the inhibitor binds in one of them.
LAT has evolved to accommodate a wide range of substrates and inhibitors.
LAT has two distinct binding modes and the inhibitor binding is dependent on the conformational changes induced by the inhibitor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the binding modes of the substrate and the inhibitor are distinct, and LAT exhibits a unique mechanism for substrate recognition and binding.
LAT inhibitors may be designed to target the binding modes of the substrate, the cofactor and the inhibitor.
LAT is a unique enzyme that can be targeted to develop novel antimicrobials.
